title: Two dice rolled 1000 times
intro: Two fair dice have 36 equally likely ordered outcomes, and 6 of them sum to 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). So the theoretical probability of a 7 is 6/36 = 0.1667. The computer rolls the pair 1000 times (seed 1) and got a 7 in 168 rolls, an experimental probability of 0.168. The second figure compares every sum from 2 to 12 with its share of the 36 outcomes.
